title: 6.30.2 Sub-build: Crown a king
description: One red piece steps up the board; on the top row it becomes a king, 'R', which may also step back down.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: Click the red piece, then a square one up and one across: it steps up the board. On the top row it is stuck, because it may only step up.

steps.title: Crown it
steps.instructions: Where the piece has just moved (after `picked = false;`), add `if (pr === 0) piece = 'R';`. At the very end of `draw()`, show the crown: `if (piece === 'R') text('K', pc * CELL + CELL / 2 - 6, pr * CELL + CELL / 2 + 7, 20, 'gold');`. Run and step to the top: a gold K appears.
hints: Row 0 is the top row: red moves up, so that is its far side.

steps.title: A king steps down too
steps.instructions: Below `const up = r === pr - 1;`, add `const down = r === pr + 1;`. In the `else if`, change `up` to `(up || (down && piece === 'R'))`. Run: a plain piece still only goes up, and the king steps down as well.
hints: The brackets matter: "up, or (down and a king)".

requirements.title: Crowned on the top row
requirements.description: A piece that reaches row 0 becomes 'R'. Help: 6.30.1 (Reading: Kings, and a player with no move)

requirements.title: A king may step back
requirements.description: A king, and only a king, may also move down a row. Help: 6.30.1 (Reading: Kings, and a player with no move)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Sub-build: Crown a king". The task: when the piece lands on row 0 it becomes 'R', a king (drawn with a K); a plain piece only steps up, and a king may also step down one row. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries, nested ifs, switch statements and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.

rubric.title: Back down
